messages:
sofia: Heads-up — onboarding aurora-xxl-65b to staging now. Can someone do a quick pass on weights location, kv-cache format, and max_ctx so we don't hit OOMs in canary? Saw a tokenizer pad shift in an earlier run.

mike: Thanks. What S3 path are we using for the weights? size estimate?

jia: s3://redwood-models/aurora-xxl/2026-03-16/v1/weights.tar (≈ 420GB unpacked). Pulling to /mnt/nvme/models/aurora-xxl on staging-ml-07.

alex: For KV format — are we using contiguous or interleaved layout for this model? contiguous had fewer cache misses last time.

jia: Config we pushed has contiguous V2. Snippet:
```yaml
model:
  name: aurora-xxl
  version: v1
kvcache:
  format: contiguous_v2
  max_ctx: 131072    # requested by research for long-context tests
  kv_dtype: int16
  prefix_cache: true
```

taylor: Tokenizer note: the tokenizer file for this checkpoint sets pad_token_id=0 while our serving runtime expects pad_token_id=1 for chunk alignment. That causes a 1-token shift on chunk boundaries during prefix-cache lookups. Quick fix: set `tokenizer.pad_token_id = 1` during load or use `truncation_side='left'` when chunking.

mike: Re: max_ctx=131k — that sounds dangerous for a single-GPU footprint. Any estimate of per-GPU KV mem?

jia: Rough calc: for int16 KV, per-token KV ~ 192 bytes (both key+value + overhead) => 131k * 192 ≈ 25.1 GB GPU memory just for KV (per replica). With model activations + weights we need 40+ GB per replica. Staging cluster has A100-80gb but with two model shards we hit 90% GPU.

sofia: Proposed mitigation: run canary at reduced max_ctx 65536 and enable prefix_cache so most long prefixes hit cache. Also set rollout to 10% and enable auto-fallback to quantized variant if GPU mem > 85%.

alex: Agree. Also let's set `kvcache.format_check: strict` in the serving config so incompatible formats fail early instead of corrupting KV layout.

mike: Can someone run a quick smoke generate on staging with seq=100k and post peak mem & host RSS? I can pause canary if it's unsafe.

jia: Running now on staging-ml-07 — command: `./run_smoke --model aurora-xxl --seq 100000 --batch 1`

ci-bot: staging-run-234 completed — peak GPU mem: 21.7GB, host RSS: 47.8GB, peak CUDA allocs: 19.9GB. Sequence generated until 98k then ended. Logs: /var/logs/staging/run-234.log

sofia: Nice — that peak is for current config (max_ctx=65k, contiguous_v2, int16). If we flip to 131k we'd expect ~double KV => ~42GB KV which would push us OOM. So plan: keep max_ctx=65536 for canary, add a config guard to reject requests > 65k unless customer has dedicated capacity.

taylor: Also added a tokenizer sanity check during model load that asserts `pad_token_id` is in the expected set and warns if chunk alignment may shift. PR: #4287 (small patch).

alex: Sounds good. Can we also add a runtime warning metric `kv_memory_pressure` when we go above 70% so SRE can auto-scale?

sofia: Yes — I'll open infra ticket and add a quick alert: severity=warning at 70%, critical at 90%.

mike: Approving canary with those constraints. I'll start a 10% rollout after PR merge. :thumbsup:

jia: Merged config change and tokenizer guard. Starting canary with max_ctx=65536, rollout=10%, fallback_model=aurora-xxl-quant-v1.

ci-bot: deploy/aurora-xxl/canary started — id=deploy-9801 — observers: sofia,mike,jia.

sofia: Thanks team. Follow-up: collect 24h memory/latency traces and check prefix cache hit rate. If hit_rate < 85% after 24h we tighten max_ctx to 32k for public staging.

mike: Will monitor. If anything trips I'll ping here and flip rollback.

taylor: Small note to doc: added a short troubleshooting blurb under eng-ml/wiki -> "tokenizer-pad-id-shift".

sofia: Great, closing this handoff. :white_check_mark:
